rework.notes: Two defects in the B12-006 half and six in the B12-007/008/009 half were in content this cycle authored itself and were found by reading the extracted text of the shipped artifacts before release (four in B12-008: the at-risk label, the worked-example arithmetic, the 'Dashboard' cross-reference, the one-day/two-days date claim; two in B12-009: 'a eye', 'section six'). Ten were pre-existing: the Cycle-104 gate's thin-depth findings across four products, B12-008's single-formula workbook, the B12-006 typed share, and the probe's formula count, which undercounted 128 as 117. No defect reached a customer; all four products remain unpublished. The B13-001 half added five defects in content this cycle authored itself: a self-referencing variance, a change-order total that read only the first row, a percentage that divided the wrong two numbers, an allowance check that could not fail, and a status formula with unbalanced parentheses that made Excel refuse to open the file. All were found before release by the native probe or by reading the recalculated text, and the example's forecasts were corrected in the same pass because they double-counted committed money. A separate process incident destroyed an uncommitted B12-004 repair by importing the batch-12 builder; the repair was rebuilt and re-verified, and the import path is now guarded. Re-running the whole touched suite also exposed a flaky assertion in the previous half: tests/test_b12_006_repair.py::test_build_is_deterministic compared raw XLSX bytes, but openpyxl stamps docProps/core.xml with the wall-clock time, so it passed only when two builds landed in the same second. It now compares every cell value and number format, plus a new test proving the build timestamp is the only ZIP member that may differ.
